name: hand-limit-9
description: THE HAND LIMIT AT 9, AGAINST THE SHIPPED 7 (03/09/2026). The loose arm of the pair that brackets 7, and it asks the question the 12 -> 7 move assumed the answer to: how much of the free-Draw dominance was the ceiling being ABSENT, and how much is it about where the ceiling sits? Nine is five above the 4-card opening hand - still a brake, but a seat can bank two turns of draws before it bites. If this arm plays the same as 7 on the bonus mix and on the hook, then 7 is doing nothing 9 could not do and the tighter number is costing the design a resource for no return; if instead the neighbour-visit share falls and the free Draw 1 rises at 9, the diminishing-return story is confirmed and 7 is a real design value rather than a convenient one. READ: the bonus mix with the visit counted separately from the self-visit; the median and maximum hand, because a maximum that never reaches 9 makes this arm measure nothing; the boundary discard rate; and the WORST LEGAL-MOVE COUNT, which is what the rule bounds - C(8,4) is 70 payments for one buildable card against C(6,4)'s 15, so 9 is roughly five times the worst-case branching of 7 and slower to run for that reason alone. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved. ⛔ DELIVERY MEEPLE PINNED 14/09/2026: Dean ruled the delivery meeple ON as the shipped default (rules.turn.deliveryMeepleSpace 1, meepleSpendTiming 'afterAction', meepleSpendPerTurn 1, meepleSpendDistinctColours false) together with two new island rules, the space choice (rules.turn.deliverySpaceChoice true: a delivery names either free space) and the closing draw (rules.turn.closingDrawPerCrate 1: filling a tile draws one card per crate). This overlay predates it, so all six leaves are pinned here BY NAME at their pre-ruling values (deliveryMeepleSpace null, meepleSpendTiming 'start', meepleSpendPerTurn null, meepleSpendDistinctColours false, deliverySpaceChoice false, closingDrawPerCrate 0; 'start' and null are the old inert values, not 'none' and 0) and it still replays its own game.
